claims.text: Controlled cold working or pre-straining introduces lattice strain and lattice distortions into an MPEA while preserving its chemical composition.
Pre-strain-induced lattice strain suppresses key diffusion pathways in MPEAs.
Suppressing diffusion through lattice strain slows high-temperature oxidation kinetics.
Pre-strain-induced lattice strain enhances oxide-scale integrity during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The proposed behavior holds from 900°C to 1200°C for oxidation durations up to approximately 120 hours.
Pre-straining produces enhanced defect density and nanocrystallization.
Nanocrystallization creates a high density of grain boundaries.
Lattice distortion increases vacancy formation energy and aluminum migration barriers.
Pre-strain-induced lattice distortion increases chromium migration barriers at the oxide-alloy interface.
Elevated aluminum diffusion barriers suppress outward aluminum transport toward the oxidation front.
Pre-strain-induced lattice strain suppresses inward oxygen diffusion.
Restricted diffusion produces a thinner and more continuous oxide scale.
A protective duplex scale can consist of an inner Al2O3 layer and an outer MnCr2O4-containing layer.
Lattice-strain-mediated diffusion suppression makes the oxide scale more adherent.
Relative to an as-processed control, pre-strained samples will have lower parabolic oxidation-rate constants.
Relative to an as-processed control, pre-strained samples will have reduced oxide-scale thickness.
Relative to an as-processed control, pre-strained samples will exhibit improved scale adhesion.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries can act as short-circuit pathways that accelerate diffusion and promote rapid formation of a continuous Al2O3 layer.
Reactive-element yttrium can improve scale adhesion through interfacial Y2O3 pinning.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis associates enhanced defect density and nanocrystallization with diffusion suppression, while the cited nanocrystalline mechanism identifies the resulting grain boundaries as short-circuit diffusion pathways that accelerate transport. The hypothesis does not distinguish the barrier-raising lattice-distortion effect from the transport-enhancing grain-boundary effect.

The stated FeNiCuAl-based baseline does not explicitly contain Mn or Cr, yet the proposed mechanism invokes chromium diffusion and an outer MnCr2O4 layer. The qualifier 'or similar composition' does not define when those elements are present.
